summary: Kamil Zvelebil (1927–2009) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University (~1946–1952). He held posts at the Oriental Institute, ASCR (~1952–1970) and Utrecht University (1980–1990).

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who taught at Banaras Hindu University (~1959–1999) and served as an Advisor at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (~2003).

Kammie Takahashi, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at Mount Holyoke College (~1995–1999) and the University of Virginia (~2001–2009) under David Germano and Paul Groner. She held a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.

Kanai Lal Hazra (b. 1932) studied Buddhist studies and history under Sukumar Sengupta and earned a Ph.D. at the University of Ceylon under Sirima Kiribamune (~1964–1968). He served as Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta (~1970–1997).
Kanchu Onoue is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and held a professorship at Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).

Kang-nam Oh is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and under Yun-hua Jan (attested 1976). He later held a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).
Kang-yuan Sung, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Calgary (MA attested 1999) under supervisor A. W. Barber and teacher Leslie S. Kawamura.
Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied under Takamatsu Yoshie and at the University of Paris. He later held an appointment at Tokyo National Museum.
Kanoko Tanaka, an Indology and religious studies scholar, studied under traditional teacher Muni Tulsi. She served as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).
Kansei Tamura (1928–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1962) and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1962).

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Delhi (~1944–1948), the University of Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University. She was Academic Director at IGNCA (~1987–2000).

Karel Werner (1925–2019) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He taught at Durham University and the University of Cambridge in 1968, and was an Honorary Professorial Research Associate at SOAS University of London (~1993–2019).

Karen C. Lang studied at Banaras Hindu University, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg and Ngawang Dhargyey. She served as a professor at the University of Virginia.
Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a religious studies scholar who completed studies at Smith College (~1960–1964), Union Theological Seminary (~1964–1966), and Temple University (~1970–1976).

Karen Nelson Villanueva, a scholar of philosophy and religious studies, completed a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2013) and studied under traditional teachers Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.
Karen Nero held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (~2008) and the University of Otago.

Karen O'Brien-Kop is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD at SOAS University of London. She worked as a senior teaching fellow at SOAS and lectured at the University of Roehampton (attested 2020).

Karin Meyers is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Jay L. Garfield. She served as assistant professor and MA director at the Centre for Buddhist Studies at Kathmandu University's Rangjung Yeshe Institute.
Karin Preisendanz (b. 1958) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She held a post at the University of Hamburg (~1993–1997) and served as a professor at the University of Vienna (~1997–2023).

Karl Brugmann (1849–1919) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Georg Curtius (~1867–1871). He held professorships at the University of Freiburg (~1884–1887) and Leipzig University (~1887–1919), where he succeeded Curtius.
